body.en: To prove the prophecy wrong, the king resolves to *kill a hundred* tigers, believing that if he survives the hundredth, fate will be defeated. He bans tiger hunting by anyone else in the state. Within about ten years he has killed seventy tigers, and the tigers of Pratibandapuram are wiped out.

He bans tiger hunting by anyone else
In about ten years he kills seventy tigers
A British officer asks to hunt a tiger and is refused
To save his throne the king sends diamond rings to the officer's wife
He marries a princess from a state with many tigers

explanation.en: Each step shows power being misused, and bribery and fear among the officials.

body.en: A high-ranking British officer wants to hunt a tiger and be photographed with it; the king refuses. To save his throne he sends fifty expensive diamond rings to the officer's wife, who keeps all of them. Then he marries a princess from a state with many *tigers* so that he can hunt on every visit to his in-laws, and his count reaches ninety-nine.

problem.en: Why did the Maharaja marry a princess from a particular state?

steps.en: Problem: no tigers left in Pratibandapuram.
Solution: a bride from a state with many tigers.
Result: he hunted on visits to his in-laws.

answer.en: Tigers had disappeared from Pratibandapuram, so the king chose a bride from a state with a large tiger population. Each visit to his father-in-law gave him a chance to hunt, showing that even marriage served his obsession.
